# Independent audit: compactness and attained ordinary section-weight minima

Read all six sections of `candidate 62c2d01f5a0e7e2a` independently. **PASS.** This proves attainment for the specified ordinary fixed-normal problem, not a classification of minimizers or the target numerical bound.

The positive-spanning assumption gives a conic representation of every separating normal by at most two listed normals. The elementary coefficient-elimination argument is valid for either sign pattern of the dependence. If the source is not interior, these two closed caps cover K, contradicting their combined bound 2c|K|<|K|. This includes separation at source-boundary points and one-normal representations.

For the radius estimate, the two triangles with base [0,Re] and the positive and negative perpendicular extrema have disjoint interiors and total area RW/2. Thus W<=2k/R. The selected opposite-facing listed normals cover K outside |e.x|<=TW, whose area is at most 2TW^2. Rearrangement gives exactly R^2<=8Tk/(1-2c), even if this strip happens to be wider than K. Positive spanning and compactness of the unit circle justify kappa>0.

After area normalization, the common outer ball yields a Hausdorff subsequence. A zero-area limit is impossible by outer parallel sets and continuity from above of finite area. For the resulting body with interior, indicators converge off its null boundary, so its area and all fixed-halfspace cap areas converge. The closed cap constraints survive and the earlier separation argument forces the original source back into the limit interior. Source interior is therefore proved, not assumed to persist.

If rho B is inside the limit body about zero, Hausdorff support-function bounds imply (1-e/rho)K subset K_j subset (1+e/rho)K. Intersecting fixed source lines sandwiches their actual chord lengths by the same factors. This proves normalized section continuity and therefore continuity and attainment of every inverse-section objective. It does not use the generally false section continuity at a collapsing boundary. The canonical centered triangle supplies the stated nonempty feasible class.

The structural statement correctly uses only the already audited contact-star mutation: a minimizing selected chord endpoint must have a flat exposed face reaching another cut line. A minimizer of the minimum of the weights also minimizes any weight attaining that minimum there. Neither a polygonal shape nor a bounded number of faces follows.

Finally the least support value rho is the original-source inradius. Reversing a minimizing support normal places the missed two-cap region in a strip of width rho. Its mass is at least (1-2c)k, while the common outer ball bounds its area by 2Rrho. This proves rho>=(1-2c)k/(2R), and the radius estimate gives rho^2>=(1-2c)^3k/(32T). All constants and signs are correct, including a one-normal representation.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
